sections.title: Overview
blocks: A **blue naevus** is a benign collection of pigment-producing **dermal melanocytes**. It appears as a steel-blue, firm, dome-shaped papule, usually under 1 cm, often appearing in childhood or adolescence.

sections.title: Aetiology: causes and risk factors
blocks: Melanocytes arrested in the dermis during their embryonic migration; GNAQ/GNA11 mutations. The colour is blue because deep pigment scatters back mainly blue light (**Tyndall effect**).

ul: **"Blue moles are bruises or tattoos"**: a persisting blue papule without trauma is often a blue naevus, but must be stable.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: Melanocytes that **stopped in the dermis** during development produce pigment deep in the skin.

mech.t: Melanocytes travelling from the neural crest to the epidermis stop in the dermis.
A mutation drives a small clonal proliferation.
Deep pigment scatters blue light back to the eye.
mech.caption: Deep dermal pigment looks blue (Tyndall effect); superficial pigment looks brown.

histo: Dendritic, heavily pigmented melanocytes and melanophages in the dermis; cellular blue naevus has nodules of spindle cells.

ul: Uniform slate- or steel-blue dome papule.
Head and neck, backs of hands and feet, buttocks.
**Cellular blue naevus**: larger (over 1 cm), often on the buttocks or scalp.

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: Clinical with dermoscopy (structureless homogeneous blue pigmentation). Excise if new in an adult, changing or large.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses
blocks: **Nodular or metastatic melanoma** (can look blue), traumatic tattoo, venous lake, pigmented BCC, angiokeratoma.

ul: Refer if new in an adult, enlarging, or over 1 cm (cellular blue naevus; melanoma differential).

ladder.t: Dermatology via the suspected cancer pathway; excision for histology.

refer.t: New, enlarging or >1 cm blue lesion in an adult.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: New or changing blue papule in an adult, or a history of melanoma (metastasis looks blue): **suspected cancer pathway**.
Rarely, malignant blue naevus (melanoma arising in a blue naevus).
Stable for life in almost all.

pearls: Blue = deep pigment (Tyndall effect); brown = pigment near the surface.

quiz.q: Why does a blue naevus look blue?
quiz.a: Deep dermal pigment scatters blue light (Tyndall effect).

quiz.q: Which dangerous lesion can look blue?

quiz.a: Over 1 cm (cellular blue naevus) or enlarging.
